evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of Ginkgo biloba extract in the treatment of unstable angina pectoris: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
evidence.summary: Ginkgo biloba is a traditional Chinese medicine extracted from the Ginkgophyta and is commonly used in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases in China.

evidence.title: The efficacy and safety of Xueshuantong (lyophilized) for injection in the treatment of unstable angina pectoris: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.summary: Objective: Xueshuantong (lyophilized) for injection (XST) isan effective botanical drug for treating unstable angina pectoris (UAP).

evidence.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on the Efficacy of Puerarin Injection as Adjunctive Therapy for Unstable Angina Pectoris.
evidence.summary: As adjunctive therapy, puerarin injection has been widely applied for the treatment of unstable angina pectoris (UAP) in China during the past decades.

evidence.title: Cardiovascular disease and amyloidosis in phase III multiple myeloma trials: a systematic review of eligibility, screening and event reporting.
evidence.summary:
Background

Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and light chain (AL) amyloidosis are important causes of morbidity and mortality in patients with multiple myeloma (MM).

evidence.title: Risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus after gestational diabetes mellitus: A systematic review & meta-analysis.
evidence.summary: Women with gestational diabetes are at an increased risk of being diagnosed as type 2 diabetes, but the postpartum screening rate is low.

evidence.title: The effectiveness of lifestyle interventions for diabetes remission on patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.summary: Conventional wisdom affirmed that diabetes was irreversible,but current research shows that lifestyle interventions may achieve diabetes remission among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

evidence.title: Improving type 2 diabetes mellitus glycaemic control through lifestyle modification implementing diet intervention: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.summary: Type 2 diabetes mellitus represents a significant health problem.

evidence.title: The Role of Circulating Secreted Frizzled-Related Protein 4 (SFRP4) in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
evidence.summary: Secreted frizzled-related protein 4 (SFRP4), an extracellular regulator of Wnt signaling, has been implicated in insulin resistance, β-celldysfunction, and inflammation associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
